p21-l01.q: What is the one thing a cable cannot do?
p21-l01.explain: A cable in compression goes slack. Every design choice in a CDPR follows from that.

p21-l01.q: How many cables must surround a point to hold it against a force from any direction, with no gravity to help?
p21-l01.explain: n + 1 for n degrees of freedom. With three, some direction cannot be resisted with positive tensions.

p21-l01.q: Why can Stringman hold its gripper with four cables even though they all meet at one point?
p21-l01.explain: A suspended robot uses its own weight as the restoring force.
options: The motors push as well as pull
The anchors are at different heights
Gravity always pulls down, acting like an extra cable that never goes slack

p21-l01.q: Stringman’s work volume per $1,000 for a 7 × 7 × 3 m room at $795 (m³)?
What did NIST’s RoboCrane gain by using six cables to three points instead of one hook?
p21-l01.explain: A single-point crane resists swing and twist poorly; six cables fix all six degrees of freedom.
options: Control of the platform’s full pose, so it no longer swings or twists freely

p21-l02.q: Length of line 2 from anchor (3.5, −3.5, 3) to a pivot at (1.0, −0.5, 0.9) (m)?
Rate of change of that line when the pivot moves at 0.4 m/s in +x (m/s)?
p21-l02.explain: −u·v, with the x component of (p − a)/l equal to −2.5/4.434.

p21-l02.q: What is row i of the length Jacobian dl/dp?
options: Minus the unit vector from the pivot to anchor i
The cross product of two cable directions

p21-l02.q: You want Stringman’s fingers at a point on the floor. Where do you aim the pivot?
p21-l02.explain: The gripper hangs on a 50 cm pole below the pivot.

p21-l02.q: The forward-kinematics residual jumps to several centimetres. What is the most likely cause?
options: The robot is at the centre
A line has slipped or gone slack, so the lengths no longer agree

p21-l02.q: At the room centre, height where lifting at 0.4 m/s needs 0.2 m/s of winch speed per line (m)?

p21-l03.q: Tension in each line at the centre of a 7 × 7 × 3 m room with the pivot at 1.5 m and 1.25 kg (N)?
p21-l03.explain: m g / (4 sin θ) with sin θ = 1.5/5.172.

p21-l03.q: What does moving along the null vector do at the centre of a square room?
p21-l03.explain: n ∝ (1, −1, 1, −1); the net force does not change.
options: Tightens one diagonal pair and loosens the other

p21-l03.q: Why can’t a robot with all four anchors above the payload be pretensioned?
p21-l03.explain: All lines can only pull upwards; gravity provides the tension.
options: Every null-space direction has mixed signs, so no internal force tightens all lines at once

p21-l03.q: The minimum-norm tensions at a pose have one negative entry, and the feasible interval for λ is empty. What does that mean?
p21-l03.explain: An empty interval means there is no all-pulling solution; one line would have to push.
options: No combination of pulling cables can hold the load there

p21-l03.q: Lowest possible peak tension at the pivot (1.0, −0.5, 0.9) with 1.25 kg (N)?
p21-l03.explain: The minimax choice, with lines 2 and 3 equal at the peak.

p21-l03.q: With a position-controlled four-line robot at the centre, one line is commanded 1 mm too long. How many lines are left carrying the load in the ideal rigid model?
p21-l03.explain: Three lines fix the point; the fourth goes slack.

p21-l04.q: Capacity at the centre of the 7 × 7 × 3 m room, gripper on the floor (pivot 0.5 m), with a 28 N limit (kg)?
p21-l04.explain: 4 T sin θ / g with sin θ = 2.5/5.545.

p21-l04.q: You lower the tension limit from 28 N to 14 N. What happens to the capacity map?
p21-l04.explain: Tensions scale with the mass, so capacity is linear in the limit.
options: Nothing, capacity depends only on geometry

p21-l04.q: Close under the ceiling, where does a four-line robot hold the most?
p21-l04.explain: At the centre the lines are nearly flat there; under an anchor one line can take the whole load.
options: Under an anchor, where one line hangs nearly vertical

p21-l04.q: Capacity at the centre with the pivot at 1.5 m and a 28 N limit (kg)?
The capacity of the lines is 3 kg at a point and the gripper weighs 0.6 kg. What can it pick up there?
p21-l04.explain: Everything that hangs counts against the same tensions.

p21-l04.q: In the point-mass model, what working tension per line gives 2 kg at the floor centre (N)?
